population.pinned_by: file name + sha16 of each receipt in rows; `check` judges the published set only, because the chain writes a new receipt every time it runs and a population that grows under its own leg would turn every round red for a reason that is not a defect

rule.name_round: the digits between _r and bm<a|b|c>_ in the file name
rule.field_round: the first of ROUND_FIELDS the envelope states, normalised: an int is itself; a decimal string is int(); an 'rNNNN'/'R-NNNN' label drops the prefix; anything else stays unnormalised
rule.dialect: the raw spelling as published: int / decimal_string / label_string / other
rule.agreement: compared after normalisation, so a string and an int with the same value agree -- the type split is published separately as a join exposure
rule.delta: field_round - name_round, only for normalisable disagreements
rule.int_keyed_consumer_misses: the receipt states a round but not as an int, so a consumer that does dict[field] or field == <int> will not find it
